newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT-Fleming becomes youngest NZ test captain.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-Fleming becomes youngest NZ test captain.

text.p: CHRISTCHURCH, Feb 14 - Stephen Fleming on Friday became New Zealand's youngest ever test captain, leading the Kiwis into the third and final cricket test against England at Lancaster Park.
Lefthanded batsman Fleming was called in to skipper the side when regular captain Lee Germon failed a fitness test this morning, NZPA reports.
Germon strained a groin muscle during fielding practice yesterday and despite extensive treatment yesterday he was unable to pass a fitness check today.
It brings to an end Germon's run of leading New Zealand in 12 successive tests since his debut in India in late 1995.
Adam Parore, who was dropped from the test side after their innings and 68-run loss in the second test at Wellington last Monday, returns to the side to replace Germon.
Parore had been the test wicketkeeper until he was replaced by Germon at the start of Glenn Turner's reign as national convenor of selectors and coach in 1995.
Fleming, who turns 24 on April 1, replaces John Parker as New Zealand's youngest test captain.
Parker was 25 years 252 days old when he led New Zealand against Pakistan at Karachi in 1976-77.
Fleming captained the New Zealand Youth side but has never been in charge of a side at first-class level.
Regarded as New Zealand's premier batsman, Fleming made his test debut against India in Hamilton in 1994.
He hit his maiden test century in the first test of the current series, 129 at Eden Park in Auckland.
His 24 tests until today have produced 1464 runs at an average of 36.6.
Fleming becomes New Zealand's 24th test captain -- in New Zealand's 250th test.
